newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Sept 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Sept 6.

text.p: -- MING PAO DAILY NEWS - Anger in China over Japan's claims to the Diaoyu islands was threatening to fuel protest action.
-- Hong Kong's Democratic Party would hold a ceremony next week to commemorate the 65th anniversary of Japan's invasion of China.
-- ORIENTAL DAILY NEWS - Executive Councillor Raymond Chi'en said businessmen nominated as candidates for the post-1997 post of Chief Executive should not be considered above other nominees.

-- TA KUNG PAO - The territory's first post-handover Chief Executive would be chosen within 45 days of the formation of the 400-strong Selection Committee, and candidates would need to be nominated by at least 50 members of the committee.
-- Peasants in the countryside around Shanghai were paying university professors to teach them social etiquette.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL - Sino-Japanese relations had worsened over the disputed Diaoyu islands. Japan was considering suspending loans to China as a result.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST - Shipping magnate Tung Chee-hwa, considered the front-runner for Chief Executive, had held discussions with a high-profile democrat, increasing speculation that he would soon announce his intention to contest the territory's leadership.
-- The Shenzhen Stock Exchange has proposed primary and secondary cross-border listings, an information exchange, and computer links with the Hong Kong stock market.
-- HONG KONG STANDARD - The Securities and Futures Commission announced yesterday that all unit holders in Jardine Fleming Pacific Securities Trust could insist on compensation.
-- Hong Kong News Room (852) 2843 6441 No text received
